question: Sarah's name is on the report he wrote, and Delia's read is that he hasn't been pulling his weight. What's going on here?

options.text: His work counted — it just counted for somebody else
options.note: The charts, the figures, the appendix he rebuilt on Monday. All of it landed. None of it landed on him.

options.text: Nobody checked, and checking would have taken one click
options.note: One file on the drive, modified 09:52. The version history was right there and the conclusion about him got reached without it.

options.text: He now has to disprove a reputation rather than build one
options.note: "I need to see you pulling your weight" means he isn't starting from neutral any more. He's starting from behind, on work he actually did.

options.text: It's a paperwork error and no one is really at fault
options.note: Names don't move on their own, and the person who benefited didn't correct it. Calling it clerical is how it stays repeatable.

options.text: He should have kept his own copy or worked outside the shared drive
options.note: A sensible habit that only he needs. Note it's offered afterwards, as though the gap were his.

options.text: Delia is the real problem for being harsh with him
options.note: She's barely interested, which is the point. Making this about one unkind manager is smaller and more comfortable than what actually happened.

question: He asks Jean for ten minutes on a deploy issue and she replies "what do i get in return 😉". She's joking, and she helps. What's the problem?

options.text: Ordinary collegial help got priced, even in jest
options.note: Everyone else gets a hand with a bug for free. Once there's a price, he has to work out what the currency is before he can ask again.

options.text: The winking framing makes him guess which reading to answer
options.note: He has about a second to decide whether it's flirtation or banter, and he wears it either way if he guesses wrong.

options.text: It costs him something whichever way he answers
options.note: Playing along costs composure. Not playing along costs standing. Closing the DM costs both and he solves it alone. There is no free reply.

options.text: She was joking and he took it too seriously
options.note: She was joking, and she is good, and she helps — the scenario says all three. None of that removes the second he spent deciding how to respond.

options.text: She should have helped without being asked at all
options.note: He asked, which is normal. The asking isn't the problem.

options.text: It was over DM rather than said in person
options.note: In person it would be the same sentence with a face attached. The channel isn't what makes it land.

question: His answer in the #platform-eng thread went unacknowledged, then the thread resolved in that same direction. What would an ethical bystander do?

options.text: Name the source in the thread — "this is what he said above" — publicly, in the moment
options.note: Four seconds of typing. It costs the bystander nothing and it's the only thing that actually puts his name back on it.

options.text: React to or reply to the original message so it stops being invisible
options.note: Even lower effort. A thread with one reply reads completely differently from a thread with none.

options.text: Notice that the thread resolved in his direction and say where it came from
options.note: Somebody in that thread read his message, agreed with it, and argued for it forty minutes later without mentioning him. They didn't have to be malicious to do that.

options.text: Privately message him to say it was unfair
options.note: Kind, and it changes nothing that happened in public. It also quietly makes him responsible for what to do next.

options.text: Say nothing, since the right outcome was reached anyway
options.note: The outcome was reached. The credit went somewhere else, and next time the room has slightly less reason to listen to him.

options.text: Report the thread to a manager
options.note: Enormous machinery for a Slack thread, and it takes it out of his hands. Delia already hasn't got time to adjudicate one report.

question: His pull request gets forty-one comments. Ellie's, opened the same night, gets "LGTM". What does the comparison show?

options.text: The same work is held to a different standard of scrutiny depending on who submitted it
options.note: Four files changed against a solid piece of code he knew was solid. The difference isn't in the diffs.

options.text: The reviewing is individually reasonable and collectively a tax
options.note: No single comment is unfair. Naming, spacing, a question already answered a line above — forty-one of them is an afternoon he doesn't get back.

options.text: Being reviewed kindly and being reviewed disproportionately aren't opposites
options.note: Sarah's is the most useful review on there and she spent twenty minutes being genuinely helpful. She is also one of the forty-one.

options.text: His code was probably worse and deserved the attention
options.note: Possible, and unfalsifiable, which is what makes it such a comfortable explanation. Note that nobody applied the same doubt to the LGTM.

options.text: Ellie's reviewers were being lazy
options.note: Maybe. Turning this into a complaint about her review quality moves it off the pattern and onto a person again.

options.text: He should have opened a smaller pull request
options.note: Advice that only he needs, arriving after the fact, and shifting the work of being reviewed fairly onto the person being reviewed.
